column1: # notes: A p+n diode in 3D on one shared tetrahedral mesh
column3: written by write_diode3d_mesh.py as a graded box split into six Kuhn tetrahedra per cell. The anode covers the p+ face at x = 0 and the cathode is a square patch in one corner of the opposite face
column4: so the current spreads in y and z and the solve is 3D. Both codes read the same file and solve the same discretization
column5: so there is no mesh check. The tolerance is 2 percent on log I. Forward bias only
column6: since a 0.4 um square of 1e16 silicon passes about 1e-20 A in reverse
column7: below where any contact residual resolves. The comparison reads the cathode
column8: on the 1e16 side. The anode sits on 1e18 silicon whose edge fluxes are so large that its residual cancels to noise below about 1e-12 A in both codes.
